title: It was never about the code
importance_reason: public: Lino's YouTube channel, in his own voice, making historical and research claims a viewer may repeat
audience: A developer or tech lead on YouTube who uses AI coding agents, or argues against them, and has heard 'you don't understand the code'. Knows roughly what a compiler is; may not know the history. After watching, they can answer that criticism with what each earlier layer's skeptics said, why the layer won anyway, where AI coding stands in 2026, and a better question: do you understand what it does, and how do you know?

youtube.title: It Was Never About the Code: Why AI Coding Gets Roasted
alternatives: It Was Never About the Code (Programmers Roasted Compilers Too)
Every New Layer of Programming Got Roasted. AI Is Next.
description: If you've been shipping code with AI, somebody has probably told you that you don't understand the code. Programmers pushed back on compilers too, in the 1950s, and on every new layer since, and the layer won anyway.
It goes from Grace Hopper's first compiler to Fortran becoming the bar, then where AI coding is in 2026, and how I verify what my agents build before it ships.

I made this video with ShipShow, my open-source toolkit of skills and plugins that lets AI agents build narrated videos like this one, end to end. The narration is my own cloned voice. https://github.com/latent-variable/shipshow

chapters.02-compiler: Nobody reads what the compiler writes
chapters.04-impossible: The four stages of the roast
